lines.text: Two teams. Two continents. And one name they share — the Lions. Tonight, two prides that turned hardship into a team meet on a single patch of grass.
But before the roar, a question hides in the firelight. Somewhere behind both these nations stands the one who keeps the roar alive. Hold on to that.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends — episode sixty-four. Senegal, versus Iraq. Group I.
The Lions of Teranga, against the Lions of Mesopotamia. Two nations that have played through hardship most footballers cannot imagine — and made the game a form of resistance.
Senegal — the Lions of Teranga. Green, gold and red, the rhythm and fire of West Africa, led by a man whose spirit means more than any goal.
Sadio Mané, the big brother from Bambali who built a hospital for his village — his nation's greatest, and still its beating heart. Beside him, young Nicolas Jackson.
Kalidou Koulibaly, the captain, a giant at the back. Lamine Camara and Pape Matar Sarr, the young engine. A pride that plays for more than themselves.
Iraq — the Lions of Mesopotamia. White and proud, the resilience of a nation that has played through war and hardship, and never once stopped believing.
Zidane Iqbal, the boy named after a legend, calm as their anchor. Aymen Hussein and Ali Al-Hamadi up front. A new generation, raised in Europe, who chose the land of their parents.
So here it is. The fire of Teranga against the resilience of Mesopotamia. Two kinds of survival, recognising each other across a single white line.
And one duel defines the night — the explosive rhythm of West Africa, against the proud, unbreakable will of a nation that simply refuses to fall.
And before the moment that holds a whole stadium's breath — stay with me. Because first, the Lions of Teranga begin to roar.
Here is how we see it. The fire strikes first. And then, the woodwork keeps a furious afternoon agonisingly alive.
Mané collects on the left — thirty-four now, but that explosive pace remains. He beats one, then another, and slides it across the face of goal.
And a green shirt arrives to sweep it home. The keeper is beaten. Senegal, one — Iraq, nil. The sea of green erupts, and the sabar drums shake the night.
Sénégal rolls round the bowl, a wall of green and gold. But the Lions of Mesopotamia do not bow — back they come, proud and unbroken, refusing the night its ending.
The fifty-fifth minute. A Senegal corner, and the giant Koulibaly climbs above everyone and meets it with his head, a second goal already written.
And it cannons off the crossbar... and stays out. The frame of the goal shudders, the green roar catches in its throat. By the width of a bar, it is still only one.
A fire that struck once, a header that rattled the woodwork and rebounded into history. And an Iraqi pride that, even beaten, never once stopped roaring.
That is our prediction — Senegal, one to nil. The fire edged it. The real match is yours to watch.
Because some nights are not about the score. Two nations that suffered more than most found common ground on the grass — and both, simply by being here, already won.
Two prides, two roars, one pitch. The crossbar kept the answer. But the pride, on both sides, roars on.
Do you agree? Comment TERANGA if the fire of Senegal was always going to win. Comment RAFIDAIN if Iraq's lions deserved so much more.

Here is the one who keeps the roar alive. Long before the stadiums, every village had a griot — who carried the people's story in his voice, and sang it back through every drought and war, so the pride never forgot how to roar. Legend sixty-four. The Griot. The keeper of the roar.
The players are the roar. The Griot is the memory beneath it. And this Legend is not just to watch — it is yours to claim.
Here is how. Go to worldcup twenty-six dot world and create your free account — ten seconds, and the Griot, Legend sixty-four, unlocks the moment you sign up.
Then pick three of the forty-eight nations, and every goal they score, scores for you. Free to play, just for fun. No prizes — only glory.
So sign up tonight, claim your Legend, and send this to someone whose team is more than a game. Hit like, subscribe — and I will see you when the next legend steps from the shadows.
